Find co-expressologs across all species pairs

Source: R/comparison.R
find_coexpressologs.Rd

Runs the comparison pipeline for each species pair. Combines the results into one edge table for find_cliques().

Usage

find_coexpressologs(networks, ...)

# Default S3 method
find_coexpressologs(
  networks,
  orthologs,
  method = c("hypergeometric", "rank", "permutation"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  use_torch = FALSE,
  pval_combine = c("max", "min"),
  filter_zero = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  rho0 = NULL,
  null_networks = NULL,
  ...
)

run_pairwise_comparisons(...)

Arguments

networks

Named list of compute_network() outputs, keyed by species abbreviation.

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

orthologs

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, hog (from prepare_orthologs()).

method

Testing method: "hypergeometric" (default, fast), "rank" or "permutation" (rigorous). "rank" scores each ortholog pair with compare_specificity() and calibrates it against null_networks via summarize_specificity(); rho0 is refused; power is the rank-test power (see summarize_specificity()).

n_cores

Number of threads (default 1).

use_torch

Logical. Use GPU-accelerated fold-enrichment precomputation for permutation method (default FALSE).

pval_combine

Hypergeometric and rank methods: how the two directional q-values are combined, passed to comparison_to_edges(): "max" (default; both directions significant – the reciprocal criterion of Netotea et al. (2014), the Max.p.val filter of the original ComPlEx) or "min" (permissive; either direction, denser edge supply for find_cliques).

filter_zero

Analytical method only: passed to summarize_comparison(). FALSE (default) keeps every tested ortholog pair, including those whose neighbourhood overlap is zero in either direction, so a pair that could not have been called still reaches the edge table carrying its power. TRUE removes them before the q-values are computed, which is what canonical ComPlEx does – it shrinks the multiple-testing set, so every q-value moves. Set by coexpressolog_null().

seed

Integer seed for the call's random draws, or NULL (default) to draw from the global RNG. Seeding here makes the call reproducible, and with it every downstream count thresholded on q_value. The seed is applied once, for the whole species-pair loop, rather than being handed to each summarize_comparison() call: one seeded stream flows through the pairs in order, so each pair draws its own uniforms instead of every pair reusing the same ones.

What a seed buys differs by method. Under "hypergeometric" it pins the randomized-p draws behind pi0, and the result is reproducible at any n_cores. Under "permutation" it pins the per-thread seeds that the C++ engines draw from R's RNG, which reproduces the run at n_cores = 1 only: above that the OpenMP guided schedule decides which thread takes which HOG, so the pairing of thread streams to HOGs still moves between runs.

A seeded call draws from a private stream and restores the caller's on exit; with seed = NULL the draws come from the ambient stream and leave it advanced. Same contract as detect_modules and summarize_comparison().

rho0

Analytical method only: reference fold enrichment for the power column, passed to comparison_to_edges() (default NULL, the median effect size of the called pairs). The permutation path always reports power = NA: its HOG-level q-value has no per-pair call threshold to measure power against.

null_networks

Specificity method only (required there): named list with one null_network() object, or a list of them, per species.

Value

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, hog, score, evalue, q_value, effect_size, power, species1, species2, p_value, n_tests, jaccard, type (power is NA under method = "permutation"). score is -log2(p_value) in bits. evalue is n_tests * p_value, the expected number of chance hits this strong. p_value combines the two directions like pval_combine. n_tests counts the ortholog pairs tested in that species pair. Ready for find_cliques or classify_cliques.

Details

score and evalue are BLAST's bit score and E-value, related as evalue = n_tests * 2^-score. Under method = "permutation" the p-value is the HOG's, shared by its pairs, and it cannot fall below 1 / (n_perm + 1), so score has a ceiling there (see pvalue_resolution()).

Methods

hypergeometric

Fast path: pair-level Storey q-values via summarize_comparison(). Appropriate when most HOGs are single-copy.

rank

Opt-in: compare_specificity() against shuffled-partner networks from null_network() (argument null_networks), q-values via summarize_specificity(). The hypergeometric test counts how many of gene A's translated partners are among ortholog B's partners, against an urn of random draws. With small neighbourhoods (top-25 lists) that urn let technically "sticky" genes, such as genes with many zeros, through as false calls; at network density 0.03 it held against a shuffled-expression null. The rank test asks where A's translated partners sit in B's full co-expression ranking, checks every other gene of B's species the same way, and reports B's rank in that contest, so a list that thousands of genes recognise as well as B is not evidence. The q-value is read against a partner whose expression was shuffled within each gene. effect_size is sqrt(auroc12 * auroc21); power is the rank-test power of summarize_specificity() at its default reference rank.

permutation

Rigorous path: gene-identity permutation via permutation_hog_test() with Besag-Clifford adaptive stopping and Liang discrete q-values. Required for multi-copy HOGs where pair-level tests are correlated.

Gene universe

Each network is built on all genes supplied to compute_network() and the hypergeometric population is the whole network (Netotea et al. 2014). Canonical ComPlEx implementations restrict expression to ortholog genes before building the networks; that changes neighbourhoods and calls, so rcomplex matches them only when the expression matrices are restricted the same way beforehand (see compare_neighborhoods()).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Fast analytical path; seed pins the randomized pi0 draws
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, seed = 1)

# Permissive either-direction calls (denser clique input)
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, pval_combine = "min")

# Rigorous permutation path with GPU
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs,
  method = "permutation", use_torch = TRUE, n_cores = 4L
)
} # }
